ns0:a.ns1:title: I.def.1: A point is that which has no part.
I.def.2: A line is breadthless length.
I.def.3: The extremities of a line are points.
I.def.4: A straight line is a line which lies evenly with the points on itself.
I.def.5: A surface is that which has length and breadth only.
I.def.6: The extremities of a surface are lines.
I.def.7: A plane surface is a surface which lies evenly with the straight lines on itself.
I.def.8: A plane angle is the inclination to one another of two lines in a plane which meet one another and do not lie in a straight line.
I.def.10: When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is…
I.def.13: A boundary is that which is an extremity of anything.
I.def.14: A figure is that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries.
I.def.15: A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another.
I.def.16: And the point is called the centre of the circle.
I.def.17: A diameter of the circle is any straight line drawn through the centre and terminated in both directions by the circumference of the circle, and such a straight line also bisects…
I.def.18: A semicircle is the figure contained by the diameter and the circumference cut off by it. And the centre of the semicircle is the same as that of the circle.
I.def.19: Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines, trilateral figures being those contained by three, quadrilateral those contained by four, and multilateral…
I.def.20: Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that which has its three sides equal, an isosceles triangle that which has two of its sides alone equal, and a scalene triangle…
I.post.1: To draw a straight line from any point to any point.
I.post.2: To produce a finite straight line continuously in a straight line.
I.post.3: To describe a circle with any centre and distance.
I.cn.1: Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.
I.cn.3: If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.
I.cn.4: Things which coincide with one another are equal to one another.
I.1: On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.
I.2: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.
I.3: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.
I.4: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the…
I.5: In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one…
I.7: Given two straight lines constructed on a straight line (from its extremities) and meeting in a point, there cannot be constructed on the same straight line (from its…
I.8: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the…
III.def.1: Equal circles are those the diameters of which are equal, or the radii of which are equal.
III.def.9: And, when the straight lines containing the angle cut off a circumference, the angle is said to stand upon that circumference.
III.def.11: Similar segments of circles are those which admit equal angles, or in which the angles are equal to one another.
III.1: To find the centre of a given circle.
III.5: If two circles cut one another, they will not have the same centre.
III.10: A circle does not cut a circle at more points than two.
III.24: Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another.
III.26: In equal circles equal angles stand on equal circumferences, whether they stand at the centres or at the circumferences.
III.28: In equal circles equal straight lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater equal to the greater and the less to the less.
III.30: To bisect a given circumference.
IV.def.3: A rectilineal figure is said to be inscribed in a circle when each angle of the inscribed figure lies on the circumference of the circle.
IV.def.4: A rectilineal figure is said to be circumscribed about a circle, when each side of the circumscribed figure touches the circumference of the circle.
IV.def.5: Similarly a circle is said to be inscribed in a figure when the circumference of the circle touches each side of the figure in which it is inscribed.
IV.def.7: A straight line is said to be fitted into a circle when its extremities are on the circumference of the circle.
IV.16: In a given circle to inscribe a fifteen-angled figure which shall be both equilateral and equiangular.
